title: Intel Diamond Rapids the 2027 Intel Xeon at Hot Chips 2026
gist: Intel detailed Diamond Rapids, the Xeon 7 platform slated for 2027 on 18A-P, built from modular compute building blocks around a Fabric Hub, topping out at 256 cores, 1.28 GB of last-level cache, 1.6 TB/s memory bandwidth and 128 lanes of PCIe Gen6/CXL 3.0/UPI 3. STH reads the 256-core SKU as a recently added roadmap response to AMD's 256-core EPYC and expects a second-half-2027 launch.

insights.claim: Intel's Xeon 7 Diamond Rapids platform is now slated for 2027 after Intel shifted its timing earlier in the year, and STH expects it to land in the second half of 2027.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Pushes Intel's competitive answer to AMD out by roughly a year, extending AMD's window at the high end of server CPUs.
insights.quote: it seems like Diamond Rapids is going to be a second-half-of-2027 part, so we have some time to go

insights.claim: The 256-core Diamond Rapids configuration appears to have been added to Intel's roadmap very recently, which STH reads as a reaction to AMD's all-P-core 256-core EPYC design.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Suggests Intel is responding to AMD's core-count roadmap rather than setting it, a marker of who currently leads server CPU strategy.
insights.quote: It seems like Intel updated its roadmap recently to match AMD’s 256 cores since AMD’s 256-core design is an all-P-core design (albeit with 512 threads).

insights.claim: Intel is selling essentially everything it makes at present, and the next-generation Coral Rapids family after Diamond Rapids is described as enormous.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Demand-side commentary suggesting Intel server capacity, not demand, is the near-term constraint.
insights.quote: To be fair, Intel is selling just about everything it makes these days, but the next-generation Coral Rapids is an enormous family

insights.claim: Diamond Rapids' architecture looks closer to AMD EPYC's style than to NVIDIA Vera or Arm's AGI CPU, despite clear differences.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Signals architectural convergence on chiplet-plus-hub designs among x86 vendors while Arm entrants pursue different shapes.
insights.quote: this looks a lot more AMD EPYC style (albeit with clear differences) than it does NVIDIA Vera, Arm AGI CPU, and others
insights.locator: Hot Chips 2026 Intel Diamond Rapids Slide 14 Diamond

insights.claim: Diamond Rapids is built around scalable compute building blocks that each connect directly to a Fabric Hub centralizing memory and I/O, with the hub itself scalable independently of compute.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Decoupling memory/IO scaling from core scaling lets Intel cover many SKUs from one silicon investment, improving margin flexibility.
insights.locator: At the heart of Diamond Rapids sits a set of scalable compute building blocks

insights.claim: Inside a compute building block, core chiplets each hold up to 16 cores and connect to a shared last-level cache on a base tile via a 3D crossbar.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: 3D cache stacking puts Intel on the same structural path as AMD's stacked-cache parts, neutralizing a prior AMD advantage.

insights.claim: Intel positions Diamond Rapids at the top of a mesh lineage running from monolithic ring and mesh designs through Sapphire Rapids and Granite Rapids 2.5D tile partitions to 2.5D and 3D function partitions.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Provides the reusable frame for judging whether future server CPU generations are real architectural steps or repackaging.
insights.locator: Intel walked through the mesh lineage

insights.claim: At the package level Diamond Rapids stacks two Fabric Hub tiles, 16 core chiplets, and four base tiles, with core chiplets bonded to base tiles through Foveros 3D direct die-to-die hybrid bonding and substrate copper carrying links to the Fabric Hub tiles.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Confirms Intel is deploying hybrid bonding in volume server products, validating its advanced packaging capacity investments.
insights.locator: At the package level, Diamond Rapids stacks two Fabric Hub tiles

insights.claim: The flagship Diamond Rapids configuration combines four compute building blocks for up to 256 cores and 1.28 GB of last-level cache.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Establishes the 2027 x86 core-count and cache benchmark against which AMD's competing EPYC must be measured.
insights.quote: A flagship configuration combines four compute building blocks for up to 256 cores and 1.28 GB of last-level cache.
insights.locator: A flagship configuration combines four compute building blocks

insights.claim: Sixteen memory channels feed Diamond Rapids with up to 8000 MT/s DDR5 and up to 12800 MT/s MRDIMM, targeting up to 1.6 TB/s of memory bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: MRDIMM at 12800 MT/s creates a distinct premium memory module market that DIMM makers can monetize alongside HBM.
insights.locator: A flagship configuration combines four compute building blocks

insights.claim: Each Fabric Hub provides four x16 ports where each x16 can be configured as PCIe Gen6, CXL 3, or UPI 3, plus up to 16 MB of I/O cache and two accelerator complexes housing QAT, DSA, and IAA.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Configurable lanes let one platform serve accelerator-heavy, memory-expansion, and multi-socket configurations without separate silicon.
insights.locator: This flexible I/O subsystem provides four x16 ports

insights.claim: A memory value function brings CXL memory in either one-level or flat two-level mode with mirroring, and a memory encryption engine covers both the DDR and CXL paths.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: First-class CXL tiering in a mainstream Xeon is the demand catalyst CXL memory vendors have been waiting for.
insights.locator: Memory lands in the Fabric Hub through a controller

insights.claim: The total platform I/O spans 128 lanes of PCIe Gen6, CXL 3.0, and UPI 3 plus 8 lanes of PCIe Gen4.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: 128 Gen6 lanes sets the host-side bandwidth ceiling for accelerator and NIC attach in 2027 servers.

insights.claim: Intel is adding spill-and-fill optimization instructions that expand x86 to 32 integer registers by adding 16 general-purpose registers with new encodings for r16 through r31 plus three-operand instructions, while remaining compatible with existing x86 software that recompiles without source changes.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A rare structural x86 ISA extension; gains require recompilation, so realized performance depends on ISV and distro adoption timing.
insights.locator: Intel is adding what it calls spill-and-fill optimization instructions

insights.claim: Intel replaces DRAM-resident directory state with an on-die snoop filter, preserving full ECC protection by removing directory storage from memory while lowering latency and cutting coherence traffic.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Removes a long-standing x86 memory-latency tax, one of the concrete mechanisms by which Intel narrows the efficiency gap to AMD.
insights.locator: Coherence data also moves on to the die

insights.claim: Matrix multiplication acceleration on Diamond Rapids rides on AMX and AVX 10.2 with expanded vector instruction support.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Keeps CPU-side inference viable for smaller models, relevant to how much AI work stays off GPUs.

insights.claim: Diamond Rapids is built on Intel's 18A-P process node with an expanded device set including a dual-contact PowerBoost option, a new logic threshold option between ULVT and LVT, and 33 percent tighter skew corners.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A high-volume server product on 18A-P is the clearest external test of Intel Foundry's leading-edge execution.

insights.claim: Power management is designed at the compute building-block level with a new core idle state that retains L2 cache, priority-core turbo, MR4-based memory thermal management, and low-power L0p support over both UXI and PCIe links.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Idle and link power features matter most in power-capped data centers where rack density, not peak performance, sets deployment economics.
insights.locator: Power management is designed at the compute building-block level

insights.claim: Moving coherency on-die, stacking with 3D, and stepping up to 18A-P are the three levers STH credits with helping Intel close the efficiency gap with the competition.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete checklist for judging whether Diamond Rapids actually narrows Intel's per-watt deficit when silicon ships.
insights.quote: Moving coherency on-die, stacking with 3D, and stepping up to the 18A-P process all help close the efficiency gap with the competition.
